title.description: A brief title for the rule that should contain what the rule is supposed to detect.

description.description: A short description of the rule and the malicious activity that can be detected.

id.description: A globally unique identifier for the IOC rule. This is recommended to be a UUID v4, but not mandatory.

references.description: References to the source that the rule was derived from. These could be blog articles, technical papers, presentations or even tweets.

date.description: Creation date of the rule. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD

modified.description: Last modification date of the rule. Use the format YYYY-MM-DD

tags.description: Tags to categorize a IOC rule.

version.description: Version of the used IOC schema

files.description: A set of file patterns that represent properties of files.

c2s.description: A set of indicators of compromise that represent properties of C2 communication.

mutexes.description: A set of indicators of compromise that represent properties of mutexes.

named_pipes.description: A set of indicators of compromise that represent properties of named pipes.

events.description: A set of indicators of compromise that represent properties of events.

hashes.description: A set of indicators of compromise that represent properties of hashes.

value.description: A single value or multiple OR concatenated values in an IOC. This can be a string or an array of strings.

type.description: The type of IOC pattern. Accepted values: plain, regex. Default value: plain. If the value is plain, all characters are treated as literals. If the value is regex, the pattern is treated as a regular expression.

case_sensitive.description: Whether the pattern is case sensitive. Default value: false.

score.description: A score to indicate the confidence of the IOC. The higher the score, the more confident the IOC is malicious. The default value is 75.
